correctness.rationale: In the anchored Lipschitz polytope, oriented incidence total unimodularity and integral bounds imply integral vertices. The centered L4 fourth-power functional is strictly convex on the quotient, making every maximizer a vertex. Diameter two and tight-edge connectivity reduce vertices to binary indicators or one-part plus/minus configurations. Direct raw-moment expansion gives B_N(k) and T_{N,a}(t). Changing a zero coordinate to either ±1 strictly increases the best value when part size a increases, so only a maximal part is relevant. The parity threshold follows from exact adjacent quartic differences, and the two asymptotic thresholds follow from continuum optimization. The standalone exact-integer checker covers 58 multipartite compositions through order 8 and further sampled parameter ranges through N=300. Universal arguments do not rest on finite experiments.

value.rationale: The exact fourth power of the natural graph-Lipschitz-to-centered-L4 inclusion norm is computed for every complete multipartite graph with all optimizers, not an arbitrary finite slice. Unlike classical squared spread, the higher moment has two meaningful structural scales: a largest-part sensitivity threshold at density 1/12 and macroscopic unbalanced polarization after 2/3, with exact parity-dependent finite threshold. The problem is a motivated higher-moment strengthening of a canonical geometric graph functional and the phase distinction is not a mechanical restatement of the known variance result. Does not claim a new facet classification or a general downstream theorem.
